tasks.short: Produce educational films with reviewed script drafts

steps.what: Select equipment and establish educational objectives, audience and verified source material
Prepare scripts describing demonstrations, narration and required shots

loop.purpose: Draft a training script from verified instructional material
loop.input: production brief and its verified source material
loop.output: script draft with source references and proposed demonstrations
loop.check: Technician checks factual meaning, learning objectives, demonstrability and audience comprehension against source material
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; technician writes unsupported or confusing passages manually
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed template arranges sections but cannot write audience-specific explanations

steps.what: Verify the script and produce films through equipment setup, recording and editing
Check the finished training film and release the accepted version

tasks.design: Use a bounded drafting function connected to verified material in {DOCS} to prepare a script for review. The technician selects equipment, verifies demonstrations and produces the film in an {OTHER} audiovisual production system, then checks and releases the exact finished version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Writing a first script required turning varied source material into a coherent explanation.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded language draft can propose that explanation while keeping its source material available for comparison.
tasks.still_hard: A plausible script may teach the wrong procedure or fail when demonstrated with real equipment.
tasks.human_edge: The technician judges whether the demonstration is clear, accurate and practical to record.
tasks.altitude: More time remains for instructional clarity; publication rights and physical production duties stay the same.

reach.task: Translate a learning objective into a feasible demonstration

evidence.claim: A source-grounded script drafting loop with human verification is a plausible design; no measured saving for producing training films is established here.

assumptions: Boundary is technician work from training request to released film; trainer preparation and learner time remain outside it.
The technician produces the brief in s1, including audience, learning objectives, approved facts, source versions and equipment constraints. This capture remains fully counted.

The script loop reads that brief directly; it needs no pre-existing structured safety or suitability flag. Missing facts are requested and written manually within s1 or s2, without automatic inference.
Test available drafting configuration in the existing document environment before custom code. OTHER means audiovisual production and editing software.
No editing, filming, equipment-selection or learner-time saving is claimed. Additional source checks and script upkeep receive a separate allowance.
unknowns: Whether the existing document environment permits confidential drafting
How much script writing belongs to this technician
research_questions: Can reviewed first drafts reduce script preparation without increasing demonstration corrections?

already_counted.description: Source comparison and correction of script drafts

incremental.description: Maintain drafting instructions and verify changing instructional sources
Training coordinator resolves changed learning requirements

approvals.approved_version: Exact film master version, soundtrack, captions and release destination checked in s4; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=92.5; gross 7.5 minus 5 focal upkeep gives central net 2.5. Range covers source clarification consuming all gains versus a small repeatable script component; recording and final checking keep all their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare programme reports from checked content and schedule records

steps.what: Gather past and future programs and resolve their dates, versions and content descriptions
Prepare reports by arranging programme records into past and future sections
Check report content against source records and issue the accepted report

tasks.design: Configure a programme report in the {OTHER} broadcast playout and scheduling system, using content descriptions checked by the technician. Generate the draft in {DOCS}, preserving planned versus actual labels and source versions, then have the technician verify and issue it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports required copying programme entries and arranging content descriptions from several sources.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing schedule exports and report configuration can populate fixed sections without interpreting broadcast content.
tasks.still_hard: Last-minute changes and incomplete descriptions require direct checking with the programming team.
tasks.human_edge: The technician identifies misleading omissions and explains material differences between scheduled and transmitted content.
tasks.altitude: Less time goes into report layout; responsibility for accurate programme reporting stays the same.

reach.task: Explain material schedule changes in programme reports
reach.learn: Version control and distinction between planned and transmitted content

evidence.claim: A configured report can arrange checked programme metadata and schedule records into a fixed document; the digest supplies no measured case for this particular reporting change.

assumptions: Boundary covers technician report preparation and issue, not creating programmes or deciding the schedule.

Programming staff maintain programme id, title, content description, planned date and schedule version during normal scheduling; the playout system records actual transmission time and programme id. No labour saving is claimed for their existing runtime or work.

In fully retained s1 the technician checks those fields, records report period and actual/planned status, resolves missing descriptions and produces the checked dataset. If exports or fields are absent, manual capture stays in s1; s2 remains manual where configuration cannot use that dataset.
Test the native broadcast playout and scheduling report configuration before building an integration. OTHER denotes that system; the generator copies checked descriptions without inventing summaries.
The upkeep allowance covers mapping and report-template changes; additional programming-team clarification is counted separately.
unknowns: Whether the schedule and as-run logs share stable programme ids
Whether content descriptions are reusable and current
Whether reports are already generated automatically
research_questions: Can a native report reproduce a sample of past and planned programmes without losing content or version differences?

already_counted.description: Metadata capture and resolution of missing descriptions

incremental.description: Maintain field mappings and report template
Programming team clarifies changed programme descriptions

approvals.approved_version: Exact report draft version, reporting period, source schedule snapshot and recipients verified in s3; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=65; gross 35 minus 7 focal upkeep gives central net 28. Range covers already-automated reports with no new gain and partial reuse of structured descriptions; metadata resolution and final review remain fully counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Drafting and report arrangement take less time where source records are reliable; physical production and editorial responsibility remain with the technician.
reach: Work with producers on instructional demonstrations
Work with programming staff on traceable schedule reports
role.ambitious_version: A technician who can explain both how training content was produced and what was actually broadcast.
